newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds scoot ahead with Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds scoot ahead with Treasuries.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities pared earlier gains on Tuesday, but managed to stay above ground, market experts said.
The rise in pass-through prices was heavily supported by a rally in Treasuries, following a tamer-than-expected Employment Cost Index (ECI), they said.
The U.S. Labor department said ECI rose 0.8 percent in the fourth quarter, which was slightly lower than Wall Street expectations of a 0.9 percent rise.
In the wake of the number, 30-year Treasury bond prices shot up over a full point, taking discount mortgage-backed paper for about a half-point ride, traders said.
"Mortgages are having a good day," said one. "We've been buying 30-year conventional 8.0s and 8.5s, as well as Ginnie II 8.5s," he said.
By late afternoon, pass-through prices receded in line with Treasuries and yield spreads gradually flattened.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was up 4/32 at 99-14/32, yielding 108 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent was up 5/32 at 99-13/32, and Freddie Mac current coupons were 6/32 higher at 99-18/32.
The 10-year Treasury note rose 7/32 to yield 6.64 percent.
Looking forward, mortgage traders said yield spreads should continue to narrow to Treasuries.
"We still think we are in a trading range," said one New York-based trader.
"As long as you are in a trading range, its going to be difficult to break out -- for mortgages to really (perform) much worse," he said.
